{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer-side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and verified nineteen rules. The package is unusually favourable to us: indemnification (§ 20), IP and Deliverable ownership (§ 14), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4 / § 29.4), auto-renewal and uplift (§ 8), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19), audit rights (§ 22), governing law and venue (§ 28) and insurance (§ 18) all meet the preferred position, and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment, non-solicitation or Customer-side MFN burden anywhere in the document. Several provisions run affirmatively in our favour (Vendor-granted MFN at § 7.6, Vendor non-compete at § 12.4, indemnities as Excluded Claims outside the cap at § 21.3), and we have left those intact.

Two issues require redlines, and both sit in walk-away territory rather than merely below the fallback:

1. **Limitation of liability (§ 21) — critical.** The cap is mutual and the Excluded Claims list is appropriately broad, but "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee only (the one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form per § 1.6), and the cap is further confined to that first Order Form. That is an illusory cap far below six months' fees, and the same narrow defined term undercuts the § 21.3 payment carve-out. We have reset the cap basis to the greater of fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, and confirmed Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. All other § 21 wording, including the "undisputed" and "conforming Services" limits, is preserved.

2. **Liquidated damages (§ 7.7) — high.** Section 7.7 imposes Customer-payable liquidated damages of fifteen percent of annual Fees for every week an invoice is more than ten days overdue. It is not an early-termination fee, it is uncapped over time, and a minor payment delay can quickly generate exposure exceeding remaining contract value. We have replaced § 7.7 with an express no-liquidated-damages provision; no other clause cross-references § 7.7 or retains a related payment formula.

---

## Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** (redline proposed; repaired) | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (preferred) | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant (preferred) | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** (redline proposed) | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant (preferred) | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant (preferred) | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (preferred) | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (preferred) | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant (preferred) | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant (preferred) | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant (preferred) | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (meets fallback and substantially the preferred position) | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant (preferred) | § 18 Insurance |

---

## Walk-away items

Both open deviations were classified as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature, not trade-away points:

- **§ 21 — illusory liability cap.** Limiting recovery to the Implementation Fee (USD 12,000, per §§ 1.5–1.6) under the first Order Form only fails even the fallback cap basis. We require the twelve-month paid-or-payable / USD 1,000,000 greater-of formulation and confirmation that our payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.
- **§ 7.7 — uncapped Customer-payable liquidated damages.** Fifteen percent of annual Fees per week of delay, triggered by a ten-day payment lag and uncapped in duration, fails the fallback (sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) and can exceed remaining contract value. It must be deleted.

---

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline with our two changes: the reset § 21 cap basis and payment carve-out, and deletion of § 7.7 in favour of an express no-liquidated-damages provision. Both are presented as playbook walk-away positions.
2. Confirm to Vendor that no other clause is in play — the balance of the Agreement is accepted as drafted, including provisions running in our favour (§ 7.6 Vendor MFN, § 12.4 Vendor non-compete, § 21.3 Excluded Claims), which we are retaining.
3. On § 21, hold the twelve-month lookback anchored to the date of the claim; the Excluded Claims list already exceeds the fallback super-cap, so there is no need to trade it against the cap basis.
4. Flag internally, for commercial awareness only (no redline sought): Deliverable ownership in § 14.2 is expressed as subject to payment of the applicable Fees; the § 19.2 deliverable conformance period is ninety days rather than twelve months (hosted software is covered for the full subscription term); and the § 19.3 malicious-code warranty is qualified by "intentionally introduced by Vendor".
5. Circulate the executed redline for business sign-off on the USD 1,000,000 cap floor before it goes to Vendor.
"}
